ARTEFACT: Movable archaeological finds, portable objects, object-like remains, and groups of finds recovered in archaeological contexts. This includes pottery and ceramic assemblages, vessels, tools, jewellery, figurines, seals, inscriptions, coins, musical objects, weapons, tiles, fragments, architectural members when treated as finds, bones, ash, charcoal, and other deposited remains. Also annotate general find expressions such as «κινητά ευρήματα» when they refer to archaeological finds. Examples: «ενώτια», «σκύφος», «σφραγίδα», «κεραμεική», «εργαλεία», «λεπίδες», «αιχμές βελών», «κόσμημα», «τέφρα», «καμένα ὀστὰ», «πακτωμένη κεραμική», «ηγεμόνες καλυπτήρες κεραμίδες», «αρχιτεκτονικά μέλη». Do not annotate immovable structures such as tombs, walls, temples, wells, altars, stoas, rooms, or sanctuaries as ARTEFACT.
PERIOD: Archaeological periods, chronological phases, cultural phases, and ancient date ranges. Include the full chronological expression, including prepositions such as «από», «ως», «μέχρι», «κατά», when they are part of the date or phase expression. Examples: «Νεολιθική εποχή», «Τελική Νεολιθική», «ἀρχαιότερης Νεολιθικῆς», «κατὰ τὴν ἀρχαιότερη φάση», «μυκηναϊκή φάση», «ΥΕ ΙΙΙΒ/Γ», «από το 3600 ως το 3000 π.Χ.», «2ος αι. π.Χ.», «αυτοκρατορική περίοδος», «προ-μυκηναϊκὴ φάση». Exclude modern dates, excavation seasons, publication years, and modern historical references such as «2019» unless they form part of an archaeological dating expression.
LOCATION: Named geographical places and place names, including cities, villages, regions, countries, islands, bays, rivers, ancient place names, museums, and named archaeological sites when used as toponyms rather than structures. Examples: «Πλωτινόπολη», «Διδυμότειχο», «Έβρος», «Αἰτωλία», «ἀρχαῖο Μολύκρειον», «Ραμνοῦς», «Λαδοχώρι», «Φιγάλεια», «όρμος του Αγίου Ιωάννη», «Αρχαιολογικό Μουσείο Ιωαννίνων». Do not annotate archaeological structures such as temples, sanctuaries, tombs, wells, walls, stoas, agoras, acropoleis, or cemeteries as LOCATION, unless the expression functions primarily as a place name. Exclude personal names of archaeologists, researchers, authors, and excavators.
CONTEXT: Immovable archaeological contexts, built spaces, architectural structures, and in situ parts of structures. This includes temples, sanctuaries, wells, walls, tombs, rooms, altars, stoas, agoras, acropoleis, cemeteries, deposits, farmhouses, buildings, hostels, foundations, floors, corners of buildings, wall parts, architectural spaces, and structural architectural members when they are part of a building or monument. Examples: «τάφος», «τοίχος», «βωμός», «πηγάδι», «χείλος», «καμαροσκέπαστος θάλαμος», «ἀποθέτης», «αγροικία», «ἀκρόπολη», «Ιερό του Πανός», «ἱερὸ τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς καὶ τοῦ Ποσειδώνα», «Διοικητικό κτίριο», «Ξενώνας», «θεμέλια τοίχου», «δάπεδα τῶν οἰκιῶν», «παραστάδες», «επιστύλιο», «γείσο». Prefer the complete meaningful structure span, especially coordinated names such as «ἱερὸ τῆς Ἀθηνᾶς καὶ τοῦ Ποσειδώνα». Do not annotate named geographical places as CONTEXT. Do not annotate loose fragments, portable finds, ash, bones, ceramics, tiles, or general natural surfaces such as «έδαφος» as CONTEXT unless they denote an in situ archaeological layer or structure.
MATERIAL: Specific materials, substances, rocks, minerals, clays, metals, animal-derived materials, shells, pigments, and material adjectives from which artefacts, structures, or finds are made. Examples: «μάρμαρο», «λίθος», «λίθο», «λίθους», «πηλός», «άργιλος», «χαλκός», «οξείδιο του χαλκού», «οστό», «οστέινος», «πήλινη», «μαλαχίτης», «Spondylus gaederopus», «ὀγκόλιθοι», «λιθόπλινθοι». Annotate material adjectives separately from artefacts when they simply indicate material, e.g. «πήλινη» + «σφραγίδα». Do not annotate broad generic expressions such as «πρώτες ύλες» or «αλλόχθονες πρώτες ύλες» unless a specific material is named. If bones, ash, ceramics, tiles, or fragments are described as deposited finds rather than as the substance of another object, annotate them as ARTEFACT instead of MATERIAL.
SPECIES: Animal and plant species, including real, symbolic, and mythological animals when they denote living beings or depicted creatures. Include parenthetical or synonymous species terms when present. Examples: «αγελάδα», «μοσχαράκι», «λιοντάρι», «λιονταράκι», «σκύμνος», «φίδι», «γρύπας». If the animal or plant term denotes the material of an object, such as shell, bone, ivory, or wood used as material, annotate it as MATERIAL instead of SPECIES. Do not annotate personal names or divine figures as SPECIES.
PERSON: Historical, mythological, divine, or legendary figures mentioned as persons or named beings. Examples: «Αλέξανδρος», «Αλέξανδρος ο Μέγας», «Αθηνά», «Ποσειδώνας», «Απόλλων», «Αφροδίτη», «Κυβέλη», «Σφίγγα». Include inflected forms such as «Αλεξάνδρου» or «Ποσειδώνα». Exclude modern archaeologists, researchers, authors, excavators, and scholars, such as «Βασίλειος Πετράκος» or «Στάης», unless the project explicitly requires modern persons. Do not annotate personal names as LOCATION or CONTEXT.
FEATURE: Stylistic, typological, iconographic, decorative, technical, morphological, or shape/type characteristics of artefacts, figures, structures, or artistic representations. Examples: «κιβωτιόσχημος», «αδιακόσμητη», «διακοσμημένη», «ερυθρόμορφο», «ανάγλυφη διακόσμηση», «ένθρονη μορφή», «ανθρωπόμορφα», «ζωόμορφα», «δακτυλιόσχημη βάση», «μονόχρωμος», «ἡμισφαιρικός», «καμαροσκέπαστος». Do not annotate materials, chronological periods, place names, persons, or architectural elements themselves as FEATURE. Architectural members such as «παραστάδες», «επιστύλιο», and «γείσο» should be CONTEXT when they are structural parts of a monument. Do not annotate abstract narrative terms such as «θρύλοι», «μύθοι», «δοξασίες», «γεγονότα», or «βίος» as FEATURE.
